body_text:
The Invariance of Dimension. Any two bases of a vector space $V$
over a field $F$ have the same cardinality. This unique cardinal
number is the *dimension* $\dim_F(V)$.

*Proof Sketch (Finite Dimensions)*: The result rests on the
*Steinitz Exchange Lemma*: if $\{u_1, \dots, u_m\}$ is linearly
independent in $V$ and $\{w_1, \dots, w_n\}$ spans $V$, then
$m \leq n$, and one can successively exchange $m$ vectors from
$\{w_j\}$ with $\{u_i\}$ such that the resulting set still spans
$V$. If $B_1$ and $B_2$ are two bases of sizes $n_1$ and $n_2$,
then $B_1$ is independent and $B_2$ spans, so $n_1 \leq n_2$.
Symmetrically, $B_2$ is independent and $B_1$ spans, so
$n_2 \leq n_1$. Hence $n_1 = n_2$.

Consequently, every linearly independent set in an $n$-dimensional
space has cardinality at most $n$, and every spanning set has
cardinality at least $n$.
